definitions: An English poet (c. 1552/1553 – 1599) known for his epic poem The Faerie Queene, which celebrates Queen Elizabeth I.
A significant figure in the Elizabethan era, often considered one of the greatest poets in the English language.
examples: Edmund Spenser's work influenced many later poets.
The Faerie Queene is Edmund Spenser's most famous contribution to literature.
Students often study Edmund Spenser in courses on Renaissance literature.
